text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- United Nations Secretary-General Kofi Annan wants to avoid half finished dialogues in attempts to resolve the Cyprus dispute.
- Russian tourists were 6.7 percent of the tourism market to Cyprus in 1996, according to travel industry statistics.
- "I hate failure, but it is possible in Cyprus," says Richard Holbrooke, the newly appointed U.S. presidential emissary on the Cyprus dispute.
- Disagreements of political parties were voiced yesterday on government tactics leading up to the direct talks in New York next month with the Turkish Cypriot side.

- Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash rejected suggestions by Ankara that he be flexible on territorial aspects of the Cyprus dispute in return for securing separate sovereignty for the Turkish Cypriot community of Cyprus.
- Acceptance of a United Nations set of ideas on the Cyprus problem is the main stumbling block among opposition parties forging an alliance in next year's presidential elections.
